name: FPGA & Bitstream Security Assessment
description: Covers security assessment of FPGA-based designs and their configuration. Includes review of bitstream encryption and authentication configuration, evaluation of key storage options (battery-backed RAM, eFuse, PUF-derived keys), exposure of configuration and readback interfaces (JTAG, SelectMAP, SPI configuration flash), and evaluation of vendor security features such as tamper monitors and anti-readback controls. Side-channel extraction of bitstream keys belongs to HWSEC-SCA-DPA.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to FPGA or bitstream security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands FPGA configuration and the threats to bitstream confidentiality and integrity
evidence: Can explain how an FPGA is configured from external flash and what a bitstream contains
Understands the difference between bitstream encryption and bitstream authentication
Aware of key storage options and known classes of bitstream attacks (cloning, readback, key extraction, tampering)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Reviews FPGA security configuration under supervision
evidence: Extracts the bitstream from configuration flash and identifies whether it is encrypted or authenticated
Reviews vendor security settings (readback disable, JTAG lock, key source) against a checklist with guidance
Identifies configuration and debug interfaces on a target board
Documents findings in the lab's reporting template

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses FPGA design security and configuration
evidence: Evaluates the bitstream protection configuration against vendor guidance and the product's security claims
Assesses key storage choice and provisioning process for exposure and lifecycle risks
Tests configuration, readback and debug interface exposure and determines what an attacker can obtain
Produces findings that distinguish configuration weaknesses from inherent device limitations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Evaluates advanced FPGA security architectures; reviews assessments; mentors team
evidence: Assesses SoC FPGA secure boot chains combining processor and fabric configuration
Evaluates the susceptibility of bitstream decryption to side-channel and fault attacks and scopes follow-up testing
Technically reviews FPGA security assessment reports
Mentors analysts on FPGA architectures and vendor security features

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognised authority on FPGA security; defines methodology; advises vendors
evidence: Defines the lab's FPGA and bitstream security assessment methodology
Publishes research on FPGA bitstream security or reverse engineering
Advises FPGA vendors and integrators on secure configuration architecture
Evaluates new device families and their security features for lab readiness

assessment_methods.description: Given an FPGA-based target board, determine the bitstream protection configuration, assess configuration and readback interface exposure, and report weaknesses with recommended configuration changes
Review an FPGA security assessment report for correct interpretation of vendor security features, coverage of key storage and interface exposure, and justified findings

equipment: SPI flash programmer and test clips for configuration memory
